city_fields.supportSceneAlt: Pregnant mother consulting with her doula in Cumming, Georgia
city_fields.culture: Cumming is the county seat of Forsyth County, Georgia, a suburban city of about 7,300 residents at the heart of one of the fastest-growing counties in the state. Families here are drawn to the area's school system, parks like the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, and a growing Main Street district with local shops and restaurants. The Forsyth County birth community is served by doulas and midwives based in Cumming and the surrounding north Fulton corridor, with families delivering at Northside Hospital Forsyth in Cumming, Emory Johns Creek Hospital in Johns Creek, and WellStar North Fulton Hospital in Roswell. The county has no freestanding birth center within Cumming city limits, but Atlanta Birth Center in Midtown Atlanta offers an accredited freestanding option about 45 minutes south.
city_fields.medicaidNote: No — Georgia Medicaid does not currently provide a statewide doula benefit. As of 2024, Georgia has not passed legislation comparable to Texas SB 750 or California Medi-Cal doula coverage. Confirm current eligibility and any pilot or managed-care benefits with your plan directly, as programs can change.
